steps.name: environment-check-and-persist
steps.description: Validate node and npm availability and versions, create the workspace directory, and persist npm global bin to /etc/profile.d safely so CLI tools are available in future sessions. Export PATH for the current shell so subsequent steps see it. Operates in workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE"
command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "node not found" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "npm not found" >&2; exit 3; }
# Basic sanity: require node >=14 and npm >=6
NODE_VER=$(node -v | sed -E 's/^v//')
NPM_VER=$(npm -v)
node_major=$(echo "$NODE_VER" | cut -d. -f1 || echo 0)
npm_major=$(echo "$NPM_VER" | cut -d. -f1 || echo 0)
if [ "$node_major" -lt 14 ]; then echo "node version $NODE_VER is <14" >&2; exit 4; fi
if [ "$npm_major" -lt 6 ]; then echo "npm version $NPM_VER is <6" >&2; exit 5; fi
# Persist npm global bin via /etc/profile.d (compute at shell startup)
PROFILE_FILE="/etc/profile.d/npm_bin_simple_calculator.sh"
if ! sudo test -f "$PROFILE_FILE" || ! sudo grep -q "# added by env-001" "$PROFILE_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
  sudo bash -c "cat > '$PROFILE_FILE' <<'EOF'
# added by env-001: ensure npm global bin on PATH
if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  NPM_GLOB_BIN="$(npm bin -g 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
  if [ -n "$NPM_GLOB_BIN" ] && [ -d "$NPM_GLOB_BIN" ] && [[ ":$PATH:" != *":$NPM_GLOB_BIN:"* ]]; then
    PATH="$NPM_GLOB_BIN:$PATH"
  fi
fi
EOF"
fi
# Make npm global bin visible in current shell for next steps
if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  NPM_GLOB_BIN_CUR=$(npm bin -g 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$NPM_GLOB_BIN_CUR" ] && [ -d "$NPM_GLOB_BIN_CUR" ] && [[ ":$PATH:" != *":$NPM_GLOB_BIN_CUR:"* ]]; then
    export PATH="$NPM_GLOB_BIN_CUR:$PATH"
  fi
fi
exit 0

steps.name: dependencies-verify-and-install
steps.description: Verify package.json scripts (start/build/test) exist and ensure react and react-dom are installed. If missing, install them via npm i --save so package.json and package-lock.json remain consistent; prefer npm ci when package-lock.json exists. Operates in workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
[ -f package.json ] || { echo "package.json missing" >&2; exit 2; }
# Validate required scripts
node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); if(!p.scripts||!p.scripts.start||!p.scripts.build||!p.scripts.test){ console.error('missing start/build/test scripts'); process.exit(1);} process.exit(0);" || { echo 'package.json missing required scripts' >&2; exit 3; }
# Detect missing core deps
MISSING=()
while read -r pkg; do
  if [ -n "$pkg" ]; then MISSING+=("$pkg"); fi
done < <(node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); if(!p.dependencies||!p.dependencies.react) console.log('react'); if(!p.dependencies||!p.dependencies['react-dom']) console.log('react-dom');")
if [ ${#MISSING[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  npm i --no-audit --no-fund --silent --save ${MISSING[*]} || { echo "npm install failed for ${MISSING[*]}" >&2; exit 4; }
fi
# If lockfile exists, prefer npm ci to ensure reproducible install
export CI=true
if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
  npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --silent || { echo "npm ci failed" >&2; exit 5; }
fi
exit 0

steps.name: build-run-and-validate-static
steps.description: Build the app (CI=true npm run build), verify build artifacts exist, start a lightweight Node static server (serve.js) in background capturing PID, poll for HTTP 200 on localhost:3000, collect evidence (build size, top files, tail of serve log), then stop the exact server PID cleanly. Adds traps to ensure cleanup on error/exit. Operates in workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/simple-calculator-40856-40905/SimpleCalculatorApplication"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
export CI=true
LOG="$WORKSPACE/.build_and_serve.log"
PIDFILE="$WORKSPACE/.serve.pid"
SERVELOG="$WORKSPACE/.serve.log"
cleanup(){ rc=$?; if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE" 2>/dev/null || true); if [ -n "$PID" ] && ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then kill "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi; rm -f "$PIDFILE"; fi; exit $rc; }
trap cleanup EXIT
# Build
npm run build --silent >"$LOG" 2>&1 || { echo "build failed - see $LOG" >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOG" >&2; exit 9; }
[ -d "$WORKSPACE/build" ] || { echo "build directory missing" >&2; exit 10; }
# Write simple static server
cat > "$WORKSPACE/serve.js" <<'NODE'
const http = require('http'), fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'); const buildDir=path.join(process.cwd(),'build'); const port=process.env.PORT||3000; const mime={'.html':'text/html','.js':'application/javascript','.css':'text/css','.json':'application/json','.png':'image/png','.jpg':'image/jpeg','.svg':'image/svg+xml','.ico':'image/x-icon'}; http.createServer((req,res)=>{ let reqPath=req.url.split('?')[0]; if(reqPath==='/' ) reqPath='/index.html'; const file=path.join(buildDir,decodeURIComponent(reqPath)); fs.readFile(file,(err,data)=>{ if(err){ res.statusCode=404; res.end('Not found'); return;} const ext=path.extname(file); res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[ext]||'application/octet-stream'); res.end(data); }); }).listen(port,()=>console.log('serve.js listening',port));
NODE
# Start server in background and capture PID
nohup node serve.js >"$SERVELOG" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
echo "$PID" >"$PIDFILE"
# Verify PID is running and likely node
sleep 0.5
if ! ps -p "$PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! ps -p "$PID" -o comm= | grep -qi node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "failed to start node server (pid $PID)" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$SERVELOG" >&2 || true
  exit 11
fi
# Poll for HTTP 200
MAX_WAIT=60
i=0
SUCCESS=1
while [ $i -lt $MAX_WAIT ]; do
  HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:3000/ || true)
  if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "200" ]; then SUCCESS=0; break; fi
  sleep 1; i=$((i+1))
done
if [ $SUCCESS -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "static server did not respond in time" >&2
  tail -n 200 "$SERVELOG" >&2 || true
  exit 12
fi
# Evidence
echo "server_response_code=200"
echo "build_exists=yes"
du -sh build 2>/dev/null || true
ls -l build | head -n 20 || true
tail -n 100 "$SERVELOG" || true
# Normal exit (trap will cleanup)
exit 0

To satisfy the requirements deterministically and quickly in a headless container, I replaced the CRA-based scaffolding step with a manual minimal scaffold that produces a small CRA-compatible project layout (package.json, public/index.html, src/index.js, src/App.js) and a start/build/test script set. This manual approach meets the constraints: uses existing runtime (node/npm), keeps scripts non-interactive and idempotent, installs only react and react-dom if missing, leaves CRA CLI unused (but available), and produces a dev server via the built-in react-scripts provided by react-scripts (installed via npm). The plan preserves the original environment, dependencies, testing, and validation steps; modifies only the scaffolding approach (scaffold-001). All scripts use the authoritative workspace path, begin with the required shebang and set -euo pipefail, use non-interactive npm flags, create /etc/profile.d persistence in the environment step if needed, and include cleanup and validation in the validation step. This approach is fast, deterministic, and avoids altering global tool installations or patching CRA internals.

change_logs.message: Refined from initial version: modified env-001 to check for npx, avoid HOME-based profile writes and instead append npm global bin path from 'npm bin -g' into /etc/profile.d if needed; modified scaffold-001 to run CRA in a temporary empty dir, capture logs, ensure CI=true and non-interactive installs, and conditionally run 'npm ci' vs 'npm i'; corrected deps-001 by renaming it to install (script_name 'install'), removed jq usage and used node-based checks to install react/react-dom only if missing; updated test-001 to set CI=true, use npm test (project jest) with --runInBand and install react-test-renderer transiently with --no-save if missing; replaced validation-001's dev-server approach with building and serving the static build using a small temporary Node static server (serve.js) launched in its own process group, increased startup timeout and captured logs, and ensured clean termination. These changes address the HIGH/CRITICAL feedback items: canonical script_name, safe npx usage, non-interactive flags, reliable start/stop handling, removal of jq dependency, improved idempotency, and preserving logs for debugging.

Refined existing plan to address analyst CRITICAL/HIGH issues: env-001 (now validates npm version, safely writes /etc/profile.d/npm_bin.sh with marker, and exports PATH in current shell), scaffold-001 (pin minimal CRA template usage, robust handling of dotfiles, ensure ownership of moved files if needed, remove eval in generated App.js by using a safe evaluator), deps-001 (made deterministic: update package.json to include react and react-dom if missing, use node to emit newline-separated missing deps, run npm ci to install reproducibly), test-001 (idempotent test file creation, consider react-test-renderer as dev dep if absent but recorded in package.json optionally, CI=true enforced), validation-001 (start static server with setsid to create separate session, capture exact PID, kill that PID on cleanup, include build size and file list and tail of logs for evidence). These changes address: reliable start/stop, PATH persistence for current run, npm version checks, removal of brittle parsing and transient-only installs for core deps, mitigation of eval security risk, improved evidence in validation, and robust file ownership handling. Modified step IDs: env-001, scaffold-001, deps-001, test-001, validation-001 (scripts updated).

Refinements addressing analyst feedback: env-001 modified to write a safe /etc/profile.d script that computes npm global bin at shell startup (avoids embedding unsafe characters), validates node, npm, and create-react-app presence and reasonable versions, and confirms PATH update for current run. scaffold-001 changed to invoke the preinstalled create-react-app binary directly (avoiding npx), use tar streaming to move files preserving dotfiles and permissions, ensure shopt dotglob is set under bash, and avoid unsafe evaluators by restricting evaluator or noting risk (kept simple but validated via tests). deps-001 updated to avoid inserting '*' pins: when react/react-dom are missing it installs them via npm i --save (so package.json & lockfile are consistent) and then uses npm ci when lockfile exists. test-001 fixed module detection logic for react-test-renderer (install only when missing), enforces CI=true before running tests, and writes an idempotent smoke test. validation-001 replaced setsid launching with nohup & background capture of PID, adds a PID file, traps for cleanup, verifies PID corresponds to a node process, polls HTTP with log capture, and ensures clean termination. These changes address the CRITICAL/HIGH recommendations: avoid npx remote install, reliably track/terminate server, fix inverted test detection, avoid '*' pins, sanitize PATH persistence, preserve dotfiles, and add cleanup traps.

Replaced CRA invocation scaffold (scaffold-001) with a manual minimal scaffold that creates package.json, public/index.html, src/index.js, src/App.js and standard scripts (start/build/test). Adjusted deps/test/validation steps to work with the manual scaffold. Reason: CRA produced an internal temporary name containing capital letters causing npm name validation to fail in a non-interactive temp dir. Manual scaffold is deterministic, idempotent, and avoids invasive changes to the preinstalled CRA binary.
